children: Heartland's combination with TSB Bank is nearly complete, but Forysth Barr thinks it will need to work hard to reverse signs of sagging performance. Heartland needs final approval from New Zealand's central bank to complete the deal. Heartland hasn't updated on TSB's 1Q27 performance. However, analyst Ben Crozier notes TSB's June quarter showed a clear slowdown. Lending growth has fallen to near zero, net interest margin fell 20 basis points back to its long-run average, and operating expenditure was largely stable. "Rolling 12-month net profit is now 15% below the level Heartland quoted in its acquisition documentation," Forsyth Barr says. "Annualizing just the last six months puts net profit 26% below that level." So, improving TSB's performance is key for the merger to be successful, Forsyth Barr says.  (david.winning@wsj.com; @dwinningWSJ)
